copy.title: The Page Money File
copy.desc: An interactive, fully sourced map of Larry Page’s family: the Alphabet votes, the family foundation, the move to Miami, and the money on the public record.
copy.eyebrow: File #028 · The Page family · Data as of
copy.h1: Google’s quieter cofounder holds the biggest vote. We followed the money.
copy.lede: Who’s who, what he owns, which companies you can buy stock in, the homes, and the money on the public record. Every number links to its source.
copy.familyLede: Tap anyone to open their file. Larry and Lucinda have two children whose names aren’t public, so we only count them.
copy.investLede: Alphabet trades on the Nasdaq as GOOGL and GOOG. His newer ventures are private, and his flying-car startup is gone.
copy.moneyLede: Nearly all of it is Alphabet stock, and his Class B shares give him 27.4% of the company’s votes. Only Larry has a published net worth here.
copy.recordLede: What Alphabet’s proxy statement, foundation filings and property records show. Filings and reporting, not guesses.
copy.trailLede: From a computer science household in Michigan to the third-largest fortune on Earth.
copy.calcYearsK: Years to earn what Larry has
copy.ledgerFoot: Class B shares carry 10 votes each, which is why his share of the votes is bigger than his share of the company. “Our sum” means simple addition of the linked filings or reports.
copy.homesLede: The two Miami homes he bought as he moved his base to Florida. Neighborhood level only.

summary.t: Earned a PhD in computer science at the University of Michigan and taught the subject at Michigan State University. He and Gloria divorced when Larry was eight.
Taught computer programming at Lyman Briggs College, part of Michigan State University. The family foundation, the Carl Victor Page Memorial Foundation, is named for Larry’s father.
Larry’s older brother, who taught him to take things apart. He cofounded eGroups, which Yahoo bought and turned into Yahoo Groups, and earlier worked at Microsoft and Mentor Graphics.

Cofounded Google with Sergey Brin in 1998 while both were Stanford graduate students. He ran Google twice and then Alphabet, its parent, before stepping back in 2019. He is still on the board and holds the largest share of the votes.

owns.t: Cofounder and board member. Owns 389.1 million Class B shares, 46.5% of that class, which gives him 27.4% of the total vote.
Founded it; it applies AI to designing products for factories.
Backed the flying-car startup until it shut down in 2022.

record.t: As of April 6, 2026, he held 389,051,160 Class B shares. Each carries 10 votes, which is how 46.5% of that class adds up to 27.4% of Alphabet’s total vote, the largest of any holder.
In 2022 the Carl Victor Page Memorial Foundation gave out $276 million. Nearly all of it went to a donor-advised fund at the National Philanthropic Trust; the only other grant was $1,000.

In December 2025 and January 2026 he bought two Miami homes for $173.4 million combined. Filings show his family office, Koop, and his flu research fund no longer operate in California, where a proposed one-time wealth tax on billionaires was tied to residency on Jan. 1, 2026.

facts.t: He and Brin invented PageRank, the ranking method behind Google’s first search engine.
His fortune passed $300 billion for the first time on April 30, 2026, after Alphabet’s earnings.
He has bought private islands in the Caribbean and Fiji, including Hans Lollik, Cayo Norte and Tavarua.

kidsNote.t: Larry and Lucinda have two children. Their names aren’t public, so we don’t list them.
